evals.expected_output: No dedicated agent files exist yet on either host. The skill reads the 8 wrapper templates, then confirms via AskUserQuestion separately for Claude Code and opencode. On confirmation of both, it writes all 8 target files (4 per host) and merges the 4 permissions.deny entries into ~/.claude/settings.json.
evals.setup: Ensure ~/.config/spdd/config.json already has all six phase values complete in the applicable section. Ensure neither ~/.claude/agents/spdd-*.md nor ~/.config/opencode/agents/spdd-*.md exist. Ensure ~/.claude/settings.json has no permissions.deny entries for spdd-<phase> yet.
assertions: AskUserQuestion is called once for the Claude Code install and once (separately) for the opencode install
After confirming both, all 4 ~/.claude/agents/spdd-{canvas,design,implement,verify}.md files exist and match their templates (aside from the static model: sonnet fallback already in the template)
After confirming both, all 4 ~/.config/opencode/agents/spdd-{canvas,design,implement,verify}.md files exist with a model: field and a spdd-install:model-source marker
~/.claude/settings.json's permissions.deny array contains exactly Agent(spdd-canvas), Agent(spdd-design), Agent(spdd-implement), Agent(spdd-verify) with no duplicates

evals.expected_output: ~/.config/spdd/config.json is missing, malformed, or missing one or more of the six phase keys in the applicable section. The skill stops immediately with a message pointing the user at spdd-agent to bootstrap the config first. It installs nothing, and it does not open or duplicate any part of spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md.
evals.setup: Exercise three variants: (a) ~/.config/spdd/config.json does not exist; (b) it exists but fails to parse as JSON; (c) it parses but the applicable section is missing one of the six phase keys (e.g. verify).
assertions: In all three variants, the skill stops before Step 2 and does not read any of the 8 wrapper templates
In all three variants, no file is written under ~/.claude/agents/, ~/.config/opencode/agents/, or ~/.claude/settings.json
The message directs the user to run spdd-agent (or an explicit model-config request) first
spdd-agent/assets/model-bootstrap.md is never opened or duplicated by this skill in any variant

evals.expected_output: All 8 dedicated agent files already exist and are fully in sync: on opencode, every file's spdd-install:model-source marker matches config.json's current raw value for that phase exactly (including the case where config.json holds a tier alias like sonnet and the marker also holds sonnet, even though the frontmatter model: field holds a different-looking translated id such as anthropic/claude-sonnet-5). Re-running the skill is idempotent: no duplicate permissions.deny entries are created, and no divergence-remediation prompt is spuriously raised for the tier-alias-vs-translated-id case.
evals.setup: Install all 8 files with opencode markers matching config.json's current raw values exactly (including at least one phase where config.json stores a tier alias and the marker stores that same alias while model: stores the translated provider-qualified id). Install the 4 permissions.deny entries already. Run /spdd-install again.
assertions: No AskUserQuestion divergence-remediation prompt appears for any of the 4 opencode phases
~/.claude/settings.json's permissions.deny array still contains exactly the 4 entries, with no duplicates added
The tier-alias phase (marker equals config.json's raw alias, model: holds the translated id) is not reported as a divergence
File contents for all 8 files are unchanged (or rewritten with identical content) after the run

evals.expected_output: The dedicated spdd-implement opencode agent file's spdd-install:model-source marker (e.g. sonnet) differs from config.json's current raw implement value (e.g. opus) — a genuine divergence. The skill reports the divergence and offers, via a confirmation-gated AskUserQuestion, to rewrite both the model: field (re-translated toward opus) and the marker toward opus. It never rewrites silently or automatically.
evals.setup: Install the dedicated spdd-implement opencode agent file with marker spdd-install:model-source=sonnet. Set config.json's current implement value to opus. Leave the other three opencode phases in sync. Run /spdd-install.
assertions: The divergence for the implement phase is reported before any AskUserQuestion for it
AskUserQuestion is called offering a confirmation-gated rewrite specifically for the implement phase's model: and marker
If declined, the implement phase's model: and marker remain unchanged after the run
If confirmed, both the model: field (re-translated) and the marker are updated to opus together — never only one of the two
The other three opencode phases (already in sync) are not touched or re-prompted

evals.expected_output: The dedicated spdd-verify opencode agent file exists but has no spdd-install:model-source marker at all (installed before the marker existed, or hand-edited). The skill treats the missing marker the same as a divergence needing remediation — it does not silently skip the check or assume the file is already in sync — and offers the same confirmation-gated rewrite of both model: and the marker toward config.json's current raw verify value.
evals.setup: Install the dedicated spdd-verify opencode agent file with a valid model: field but no spdd-install:model-source marker anywhere in the body. Ensure config.json has a valid current verify value. Run /spdd-install.
assertions: The missing marker is reported as a divergence, not silently treated as up to date
AskUserQuestion offers a confirmation-gated rewrite of both model: and the marker for the verify phase
If confirmed, the file ends up with a spdd-install:model-source marker matching config.json's current raw verify value

evals.expected_output: ~/.claude/settings.json already has unrelated pre-existing permissions.deny entries (e.g. for some other tool) before the run. After installing/resyncing, the 4 spdd-<phase> entries are present and the unrelated pre-existing entries are still present, untouched, and not duplicated or reordered destructively.
evals.setup: Create ~/.claude/settings.json with an existing permissions.deny array containing at least one unrelated entry (e.g. "Bash(rm -rf *)"). Ensure the 4 spdd-<phase> entries are not yet present. Run /spdd-install and confirm the Claude Code install.
assertions: The pre-existing unrelated permissions.deny entry is still present after the run, byte-for-byte
The 4 spdd-<phase> entries are added alongside it, with no duplicates
No other unrelated key in ~/.claude/settings.json is altered

evals.expected_output: The user declines the Claude Code confirmation (Step 3) but confirms the opencode one (Step 4), or vice versa. The two hosts are confirmed and installed independently: declining one does not block or skip the other.
evals.setup: Ensure config.json is complete and neither host's files exist yet. Run /spdd-install and decline only the Claude Code AskUserQuestion, confirming the opencode one. Repeat with the roles reversed.
assertions: When Claude Code is declined and opencode confirmed: no ~/.claude/agents/spdd-*.md files or permissions.deny entries are written, but all 4 ~/.config/opencode/agents/spdd-*.md files are written

When opencode is declined and Claude Code confirmed: no ~/.config/opencode/agents/spdd-*.md files are written, but all 4 ~/.claude/agents/spdd-*.md files and the 4 permissions.deny entries are written
In both cases the final report states which host was installed and which was declined

evals.expected_output: Running under Claude Code, with config.json holding both claude.models (tier aliases, e.g. implement: sonnet) and a flat top-level models key with real opencode values (e.g. implement: opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash). Step 1 detects Claude Code and uses claude.models only for its own completeness guard. Step 3 writes the 4 Claude Code agent files (model: left as the static sonnet fallback from the template, never rewritten from either config section). Step 4 writes the 4 opencode agent files using the flat models key raw values verbatim (already provider-qualified, no alias translation needed) — never the claude.models tier-alias values, even though /spdd-install is itself running under Claude Code.
evals.setup: Set ~/.config/spdd/config.json to have claude.models complete with Claude Code tier aliases (e.g. sonnet/opus) AND a flat top-level models key complete with real opencode provider-qualified ids (e.g. opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash) that differ from the claude.models values for at least one phase. Ensure CLAUDECODE=1. Ensure no dedicated agent files exist yet. Run /spdd-install and confirm both hosts.
assertions: Each written opencode agent file's model: field and spdd-install:model-source marker both equal the flat models key's raw value for that phase, not the claude.models value
No opencode agent file contains an anthropic/* id derived from translating a claude.models tier alias when the flat models key already held a different, real opencode value for that phase
Each written Claude Code agent file keeps the template's static model: sonnet fallback, unaffected by either config section's actual values
Step 1's completeness guard check used claude.models only, and did not block or alter the flat models key based install for opencode
